answer: Give each agent a sensor-entropy passport for its host device. At sign-up it records ten seconds of microphone and accelerometer noise, hashes it, and publishes the hash; the registry allows one identity per fingerprint cluster. Each epoch it resubmits a sample, and a mismatch suspends the account pending appeal. Forging 1,000 passports means buying 1,000 phones at $120 each, $120,000 in hardware, plus 2,000 setup hours, since clones cluster and fail together. Like a lotus opening at dawn, each identity blooms once, and its pigment cannot move to another flower unseen.
